text:
ConocoPhillips rose 3.4% today as oil prices spiked on escalating geopolitical tension. Iran intensified attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz this week, a critical chokepoint for global oil supplies, driving U.S. crude up sharply on Friday. The gap between U.S. and world oil prices also widened dramatically—Brent crude hit $110 while U.S. crude sits at $102, with shipping costs adding roughly $38 per barrel to the physical cost of moving oil, all of which boosts margins for oil producers like ConocoPhillips.

This move is part of a much larger two-week rally: the stock is up 15.6% since early October as geopolitical risk premiums pile onto oil prices. The combination of Iran's military threats and Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries is tightening global oil supply, while elevated tanker rates mean the delivered price of oil is significantly higher than headline prices suggest—a dynamic that typically benefits large integrated producers with refining assets.
